title: MeshInstance3Ds using named ArrayMesh's have surface material overrides replaced with null in other scenes when saving.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.7.stable.steam [5b4e0cb0f], custom build v4.6

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable (5b4e0cb0f) - macOS Tahoe (26.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M2 Pro (Apple8) - Apple M2 Pro (12 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Saving a MeshInstance3d with an array mesh that has a name appears to incorrectly write null surface overrides into scenes which use the mesh instance. It appears to be important that the array mesh is named, as unnamed array meshes do not have this issue. This issue occurs every time you open the scene and save.

I would expect a save with no modifications to make no changes to other scenes.

I investigated this issue a little bit and it seemed like it had something to do with cache mode replace triggering a reset on the resource which fires an emit_changed with no surfaces. That resizes the overrides down to 0 which nulls them out before being sized back up.

I was able to fix this in a custom build by deferring the "_mesh_changed" call in mesh_instance_3d.cpp. I'm not familiar enough with the engine internals to know if that is a high quality fix, but that pattern also appears in VisualShader. Happy to open a PR if that fix sounds reasonable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a main scene with a 3d node.
2. Create a model scene using a mesh instance 3d root node.
3. Add an array mesh to the mesh instance 3d. Attach the make_triangle script to generate a mesh. Close the model scene and reopen it to generate the mesh. Once it is created, remove the script. Save the scene to save the mesh data.
```
@tool
extends MeshInstance3D

func _ready():
	if Engine.is_editor_hint() and mesh == null:
		generate_triangle()

func generate_triangle():
	var vertices = PackedVector3Array()
	vertices.push_back(Vector3(0, 1, 0))
	vertices.push_back(Vector3(-1, 0, 0))
	vertices.push_back(Vector3(1, 0, 0))

	var arrays = []
	arrays.resize(Mesh.ARRAY_MAX)
	arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = vertices

	var array_mesh = ArrayMesh.new()
	array_mesh.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, arrays)

	mesh = array_mesh
```
4. Give the array mesh resource a name.
5. Apply a surface material override to the mesh instance 3d.
6. Go back to the main scene and place an instance of the model in the scene then save. You might need to rotate the triangle to see it.
7. Close the model tab.
8. Reopen the model tab and save the model scene.
9. Return to the main scene and observe that the surface material override has been set to null in the main scene.

You can reproduce this behavior repeatedly by deleting the model in the main scene and replacing it. Then closing the model tab, open the model tab again and save the model.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Open the project main scene. Observe 3 yellow triangles. Open the "triangle.tscn". Observe 1 yellow triangle created from an array mesh with a surface material override and a resource name set. Save the "triangle.tscn" without making any changes. Return to the main scene and observe that the 3 triangles are now grey. Saving the main scene will save "null" surface overrides into the main scene.

If you want to see the behavior again, close the editor, stash any changes to revert the project to the previous state, then open the project again.
